purpose: Dabrafenib is used to treat certain types of cancer, including melanoma (a serious type of skin cancer), non-small cell lung cancer, and thyroid cancer. It is used specifically in patients whose cancer has a certain gene mutation called BRAF V600E or V600K. It is often used together with another medication called trametinib.
how_it_works: Some cancers grow because of a faulty gene called BRAF that sends signals telling cancer cells to grow out of control. Dabrafenib works like a targeted 'off switch' that blocks this faulty BRAF protein, slowing down or stopping the cancer from growing. Think of it as a key that fits a very specific lock on the cancer cell to shut it down.
common_side_effects: Fever (very common and can be serious), headache, joint or muscle aches, hair loss or changes in hair texture, skin thickening or warts, fatigue or tiredness, nausea, constipation, and rash. Your skin may also become more sensitive to the sun.
warnings: Dabrafenib can cause serious fever that may lead to low blood pressure or kidney problems — call your doctor right away if you develop a fever. It can increase the risk of other types of skin cancers, so regular skin check-ups are important. It can also cause heart, eye, and lung problems. Do not take it if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Avoid grapefruit and certain other medications that can interfere with how this drug works.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 150 mg taken by mouth twice a day, roughly every 12 hours. It should be taken on an empty stomach — at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal. Try to take it at the same times each day and swallow the capsules whole without crushing or opening them.
